nodes.description: State variable storing the LITI token contract address used for wrapping/unwrapping.
ERC20 private mapping(address=>uint256) tracking token balances of wLITI.
ERC20 private nested mapping tracking allowances of wLITI.
ERC20 private total supply of wLITI tokens.
Public wrap(amount) function: pulls LITI via transferFrom then mints 5000*amount*1e18 wLITI to msg.sender.
Public unwrap(amount) function: burns 5000*amount*1e18 wLITI from msg.sender then transfers amount of LITI back.
ERC20 internal mint helper that increases _totalSupply and credits _balances.
ERC20 internal burn helper that debits _balances and reduces _totalSupply.
ERC20 internal transfer helper moving balances between accounts.
ERC20 internal approve helper writing to _allowances.
ERC20 public transferFrom(sender,recipient,amount) that spends allowance and moves balances.
Caller-controlled address used as recipient of mints, source of burns and initiator of transfers.
External call to the LITI token contract pulling amount from msg.sender into the wrapper contract.
External call sending amount of LITI back to msg.sender during unwrap.
Arithmetic 5000 * amount * (10**18) computed for the mint in wrap; scales input by a hardcoded 5000 factor.
Arithmetic 5000 * amount * (10**18) computed for the burn in unwrap; must mirror the mint scaling.
Parameter amount of function wrap, supplied by the caller.
Parameter amount of function unwrap, supplied by the caller.
Local variable liti = IERC20(litiAddress) inside wrap, target of the transferFrom call.
Local variable liti = IERC20(litiAddress) inside unwrap, target of the transfer call.

edges.reason: Parameter amount belongs to and is consumed by the wrap function.
User-supplied amount flows into the external liti.transferFrom call.
User-supplied amount is multiplied by 5000 and 10**18 to compute the minted value.
Parameter amount belongs to and is consumed by the unwrap function.
User-supplied amount flows into the external liti.transfer call.
User-supplied amount is multiplied by 5000 and 10**18 to compute the burned value.
Local liti handle is created inside wrap from state variable litiAddress.
Local liti handle is the receiver of the external transferFrom call.
Local liti handle is created inside unwrap from state variable litiAddress.
Local liti handle is the receiver of the external transfer call.
State variable litiAddress is cast/read into the local liti handle in wrap.
State variable litiAddress is cast/read into the local liti handle in unwrap.
msg.sender is passed as the from-address of the external transferFrom call.
msg.sender is the mint beneficiary in the _mint call.
msg.sender is the account burned from in the _burn call.
msg.sender is the recipient of the external LITI transfer in unwrap.
wrap invokes the external liti.transferFrom call.
wrap computes the scaled mint amount before minting.
wrap calls _mint to credit newly wrapped tokens.
unwrap calls _burn to destroy wrapped tokens.
unwrap computes the scaled burn amount before burning.
unwrap invokes the external liti.transfer call after burning.
External LITI transfer hands control to msg.sender (possibly a contract) which can re-enter unwrap.
External LITI transferFrom yields control to the untrusted token/sender before wrap completes its mint.
_mint increases the recipient balance in _balances.
_mint increases _totalSupply.
_burn decreases the account balance in _balances.
_burn decreases _totalSupply.
ERC20 transferFrom delegates balance movement to _transfer.
ERC20 transferFrom updates allowance via _approve.
transferFrom reads and writes the _allowances mapping.
_transfer updates sender and recipient entries in _balances.
_approve writes to the _allowances mapping.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter amount is scoped to and defined by the core function wrap; merging removes redundant per-call parameter node.
Parameter amount is scoped to and defined by the core function unwrap; merging removes redundant per-call parameter node.
Local liti handle in wrap exists only to invoke the unsafe external transferFrom operation.
Local liti handle in unwrap exists only to invoke the unsafe external transfer operation.
